title: The auditory brainstem response to natural speech is not affected by selective attention
description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from three experiments investigating whether the auditory brainstem response (ABR) to natural continuous speech is modulated by selective attention. Participants listened to narrated audiobooks under diotic, dichotic, and passive listening conditions while cortical and subcortical EEG responses were simultaneously recorded. The dataset supports the study by Stoll et al. (2025) published in PLOS Biology, examining subcortical and cortical processing of attended versus unattended speech.
methods_description: EEG was recorded simultaneously from a 32-channel active montage (cortical responses) and a 2-channel passive bipolar montage referenced to FCz and earlobes (subcortical responses), with some subjects also fitted with an eardrum electrode. Data were sampled at 25 kHz, with cortical channels downsampled to 1 kHz and subcortical channels to 10 kHz. Participants listened to audiobook stimuli presented diotically or dichotically at controlled sound pressure levels (65-76 dB SPL) in a soundproof room, and were cued to attend to one of two narrators per trial or to passively ignore the stimuli while engaging in a distractor task.
